ground_truth.unit: percentage points (party-list turnout, % of registered voters)
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Intention-to-Treat Effect on Electoral Returns at the Barangay Level"), column 1.  Intention-to-treat effect of random assignment of a town-hall (deliberative) campaign by either party list (Akbayan or Umalab Ka) on party-list turnout, as a percentage of registered voters, from official COMELEC returns of the May 2013 party-list election, across all experimental barangays (one assigned treatment and two controls per selected municipality). Regression of the electoral return on the assignment dummy with municipality (city) fixed effects (equation 1); inference under randomization of the treatment, permutation p-value p = .404.  Not significant.

ground_truth.unit: percentage points (vote share of the treating party list)
ground_truth.context: Table 1, column 2: intention-to-treat effect of town-hall-meeting assignment on the vote share (% of total party-list votes) of the party list campaigning in the barangay, Akbayan and Umalab Ka pooled; all experimental barangays; same specification as column 1 (assignment dummy, municipality fixed effects, randomization inference, permutation p = .048).  The paper's headline result.

Table 1, column 3: intention-to-treat effect on Akbayan's vote share (% of party-list votes), barangays of the municipalities randomly assigned to Akbayan only; assignment dummy with municipality fixed effects, randomization inference (permutation p = .087).

Table 1, column 4: intention-to-treat effect on Umalab Ka's vote share (% of party-list votes), barangays of the municipalities randomly assigned to Umalab Ka only; assignment dummy with municipality fixed effects, randomization inference (permutation p = .141).  Not significant.
Number of barangays (all experimental barangays, both party lists) in the turnout and pooled vote-share regressions of Table 1, columns 1 and 2.
Number of barangays in the Akbayan vote-share regression, Table 1 column 3 (barangays of the Akbayan municipalities).
Number of barangays in the Umalab Ka vote-share regression, Table 1 column 4 (barangays of the Umalab Ka municipalities).

ground_truth.context: Supporting-information Table C.3 ("Intention to Treat Effect on Attitudes on Poverty"), upper panel (Akbayan treatment), column 1. Post-election survey respondents in the Akbayan municipalities. Outcome: the summary index of poverty-related attitudes (Anderson 2008: the four items Poverty, Gap, CCT and Corruption, each oriented so higher means more agreement, standardized with respect to the control group's mean and s.d., combined as an inverse-covariance weighted average).  Linear regression on treatment assignment with city fixed effects (equation 3), weighted to adjust for the oversampling of meeting attendees (inverse probability weights: the proportion of self-reported attendees in the survey relative to actual attendees from the meetings' attendance sheets, in treatment barangays), standard errors clustered by barangay (p = 0.017).  The surveyed municipalities exclude Imus, Pateros and Santa Maria.  The main text shows this estimate in Figure 5.

i4r.notes: Team-level verdict (code reproduces the paper's output).  Database row "appendix table c.3" (o_coeff 0.496, o_p 0.017) is the remove-weights robustness check: r_coeff 0.138 (SE 0.160, p = 0.391), not transcribed.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=0.33706 vs claimed=0.496 (relative error 32.04%, tolerance 2.00%).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Attendance weights (survey analyses): weights are built in actually treated barangays as pt/ps for self-reported attendees and (1-pt)/(1-ps) for non-attendees, where pt = att.prop (attendees / registered voters, data_agg) and ps = the share of attendees among that barangay's respondents in the analysis sample; all other respondents get weight 1. The paper only describes the adjustment verbally; this exact form is my reconstruction.

Anderson (2008) indices: items oriented as higher = more agreement with the party's concern (poverty, gap, corruption reversed 6-x; cct as is; femhouse, fempol, equality, harassment as is; discrimination reversed 6-x), each standardized by the control-group (assignment==0) mean and s.d. within the party's municipalities, weighted by row sums of the inverse (pairwise) covariance matrix over the items a respondent has, then the index is re-standardized on the control group. Effective sample = respondents with non-missing turnout_pl (1,081 here; paper says 1,082). Regressions use city FE, attendance weights, SEs clustered by barangay.
Permutation p-values, CACE and SEs were not computed (only the listed point estimates and Ns).
cell.notes: Table 1 (barangay level, eq. 1: lm of turnout.party / share.treated / share.akbayan / share.umalabka on assignment + city FE using data.all) reproduces all four ITTs and all three Ns exactly. Table F.1 unweighted individual vote ITTs (100*vote and 100*vote.akbayan on assignment with city FE, respondents with turnout_pl==1; N=890 vs 891 in the data due to one respondent with missing city/barangay) give 23.51 and 32.01 against claimed 23.242 and 31.729, within tolerance. The four attitude summary indices (SI Tables C.3/C.4) do not reproduce: 0.337/0.320/0.363/-0.017 against claimed 0.496/0.126/0.45/0.095. Attempt-2 crashed (Umalab Ka party key had a space) and was fixed. Attempts 3-5 were compared with the claims via check_attempt. Attempts 4 and 5 also printed non-RESULT diagnostic grids, which I compared with the claimed index values and with numbers quoted in the paper text (item effects, weighted vote ITTs). Attempt-4's grid varied sample, within-party vs pooled index, weights, re-standardization, complete-case vs pairwise and item orientation flips. Attempt-5's grid varied five attendance-weight schemes, att.prop vs att.prop.turn, and the base for the survey share. No variant matched all four indices, or the text's weighted vote ITTs (about 13.5 / 16.7 / 6.6) or item effects (Akbayan Discrimination 0.88). So I reverted to the principled attempt-3 specification, and the final files are copies of attempt-3. The authors' generated survey_ind.RData (which holds their indices) is not in the package, and how they built the indices and weights probably differs from the paper's description.
